title: 纳尔·远古岩原
description: 纳尔保留橙色绒毛、大耳与长尾，稳站开阔岩面，骨质回旋镖静垂身侧，远古山岭被金色侧光照亮。

art_direction.medium: angular wax-crayon strokes, directional hatching and dramatic hard-edged light on textured paper
art_direction.identity: Gnar is a small prehistoric yordle with orange fur, very large pointed ears, bright blue eyes, a long expressive tail, and a compact animal-like body. Preserve his species-specific scale and primitive opaque garment wrap rather than making him an adult human or an oversized infant mascot. His recognizable bone-like boomerang hangs quietly from one hand, never thrown or swung.
art_direction.scene: He stands upright on a broad low rock surface with both feet secure, looking across an immense prehistoric valley. The long tail curves behind him without overlapping the lowered boomerang. Strong amber sunlight catches coarse orange wax marks, while blue crayon shadow planes, a distant fern silhouette, and broad clean mountain layers make the small figure resolute rather than playful.
art_direction.palette: burnt orange, sky blue, bone ivory, dark slate
art_direction.weapon_policy: iconic static prop, no attacks or firing

visual_qa.method: up to ten images on a compressed JPEG contact sheet, max edge 1280
